title: Hamilton and Niagara awaiting results as polls now closed

image.caption: Rick McRae cast his vote at Prince Philip Public School in Niagara Falls on Monday. (Paul Forsyth/CBC)

blocks.text: A voting sign is seen outside Hamilton city hall.

items: Polls are now closed across Hamilton and Niagara, and results are expected to start rolling in shortly.
Hamilton has 13 mayoral candidates, including incumbent Andrea Horwath, Keanin Loomis, who came in a close second in 2022, and councillor Rob Cooper.
There are three open races for councillor in Hamilton (wards 8, 10 and 13) and four open races for mayor in Niagara (Welland, Thorold, Lincoln and Niagara-on-the-Lake).
You can find live results for the Hamilton mayoral race here.

October 27'They've got to keep up with the infrastructure,' Niagara voter saysRick McRae cast his vote at Prince Philip Public School in Niagara Falls on Monday. (Paul Forsyth/CBC)Rick McRae of Niagara Falls said after casting his vote that he wants action on what he sees as a growing homelessness and addictions problem. Property tax levels are a "big concern" to him, and he is particularly concerned about what he sees as not enough investments into critical infrastructure and roads."They’ve got to keep up with the infrastructure," he said. "My street has had four or five water main breaks just in the last couple of years. They put off work for so many years. You just can’t keep filling in the potholes."

How the CBC News Decision Desk makes its projectionsAndrew DavidsonHello. I'm a senior producer with the CBC News Decision Desk, a team of journalists who monitor results reporting on Election Night with the goal of making projections. Why? So we can give the audience as clear a sense of who will run their cities and communities as soon as possible. We study historical trends and consume the entirety of news coverage on election campaigns, including tips from our reporters on the ground. When the results start coming in, we watch for advance ballots and day-of votes to report, and we monitor how much the lead for one candidate grows. When we see enough separation and are comfortable with the state of the race, we can make a projection. But we don't elect people; voters do. Municipal elections generally present more of a challenge than provincial and federal votes, since there's usually less polling information available on individual races. Sometimes, the races are too close to call, and we must wait for the results to go final.We take our time to get it right. A late night just means more candy and snacks for us. We count votes on election night, not calories.

Polls close in Hamilton and Niagara municipal electionsEva SalinasHi, I'm Eva Salinas, executive producer of CBC Hamilton, here at our newsroom. The polls have now closed. City staff told us recently that they hope the first results will start appearing around 9 p.m., although the timing will depend on how quickly polling stations finish voting and report their results. We will be bringing results as soon as we have them here. You can also find live results of the mayoral race in Hamilton here.

October 26What voter turnout looked like in 2022Jeffery TramVoter turnout in the 2022 municipal election was 35.38 per cent, with 143,375 ballots cast out of 405,288 eligible voters. Although the turnout percentage fell compared to 2018, the number of voters was higher than the previous election and the highest total since 2000, according to the City of Hamilton.Peter Graefe, a professor in McMaster University's department of political science, told CBC Hamilton he is concerned fewer people may be following this election than last time. "It's hard to know whether Hamiltonians really know there's an election going on beyond the signs," he said.Karen Bird, another McMaster politics expert, said she worries about voter engagement this election, particularly among young people.

More than 30,000 people voted in Hamilton before todayJeffery TramA voting sign outside St. Thomas More Catholic Secondary School in Hamilton's Ward 14. (Saira Peesker/CBC)We're expecting most voting to take place today, but thousands of people have already cast their ballots.The City of Hamilton says 34,996 people voted during the first three weeks of advance voting, including 15,632 over the weekend of Oct. 17 and 18. That exceeds the 30,893 ballots cast over four days of advance voting in 2022. The numbers are reflective of the city's efforts to expand its options for voting ahead of election day. This includes a ballot-on-demand service that allows eligible voters to cast a ballot from a location regardless of which ward they live in. Ballots cast at advance polls and ballot-on-demand locations will be counted today.

Polling day 'snuck up on us,' voter says of a low-profile election seasonJustin ChandlerJonathan Deveau cast his ballot at Dr. J. E. Davey Elementary School on Monday election night in Hamilton. (Carlos Osorio/CBC)Jonathan Deveau, 42, voted in downtown Hamilton around 7:30 p.m. He said crime and homelessness were top of mind for him this election. He said didn’t hear many people talking about the election. "It felt like it snuck up on us."

Some candidates are already acclaimedJustin ChandlerSome candidates win before anyone even votes. That's called acclamation, and it's the process that happens when a candidate is the only one running for an elected office and wins by default. In Hamilton, more than a third of school board trustees were acclaimed, with one saying a shortage of candidates "isn't healthy for democracy."On the Hamilton-Wentworth District School Board, candidates for two of 11 seats won by acclamation:Incumbent Abby Zaitley in Ward 4.In Ward 13 Chris Slye was acclaimed when Andrea Wappel's name was withdrawn.At the Hamilton-Wentworth Catholic District School Board, candidates for four of the nine seats won by acclamation:Mark Valvasori, who was acclaimed in 2022, was again acclaimed for wards 1, 2 and 15.Ralph Agostino was acclaimed in wards 3 and 4.Incumbent Aldo D'Intino was acclaimed in Ward 5.In wards 9 and 11, current Ward 7 trustee Tyler Iorio was acclaimed.Nathalie Dufour Seguin was acclaimed for the French Catholic board trustee seat.The French public board trustee seat went to Sonia Macaluso, after the only other candidate, Pierre Gregory, withdrew.The eight acclamations on the school boards was four times higher than in 2022.The Association of Municipalities of Ontario said there were 400 candidate acclamations across the province in 2026, down from 548 in 2022 and 477 in 2018.

How will votes be counted?Jeffery TramWhen polls close at 8 p.m. in Hamilton, anyone still in line will be eligible to vote. Election workers will identify the end of the line and allow everyone present to finish voting before closing up.Throughout the day, workers feed marked ballots into a tabulator, which record votes. Paper ballots will be dropped into secure boxes.At the end of the day, the tabulators will print results showing the votes recorded by each machine.It is then sent to a central location, where the city will then start posting the results.Some polling locations experienced delays during the 2022 municipal election because of problems with software used to manage the voters' list. The system's servers slowed down, making it harder for staff to process voters quickly, the city has told us. This year, the city has an offline version of the software it can switch to if needed, along with backup internet connections and IT staff assigned to every ward.

Exciting races to watch across the regionJustin ChandlerBurlington city hall is seen in 2025. (Kate Bueckert/CBC)Had your fill of Hamilton's hot mayoral race? Things are nearly just as spicy in neighbouring Burlington, where two incumbent councillors — Lisa Kearns and Rory Nisan — are challenging the incumbent mayor, Marianne Meed Ward. With three of six sitting councillors not running for re-election, that city is sure to see new faces in the council chamber. There are at least three new Hamilton city councillors heading to city hall, as wards 8, 10 and 13 are without incumbents. In Ward 8, residents will get their third councillor in just over a year, as Rob Cooper is running for mayor instead of the council seat. In Ward 10, 11 candidates vying to replace Jeff Beattie, who ran and won a recent provincial byelection, becoming an MPP. And, in Ward 13, four candidates are facing off to replace Alex Wilson, who opted not to run again. Brantford is guaranteed to get a new mayor, with incumbent Kevin Davis not running again. There are seven candidates in that race, including three city councillors, a business owner and a wrestler. The mayor of Norfolk County, Amy Martin, also chose not to run again. There, seven candidates are running for mayor. And, in Haldimand County, three challengers are trying to beat the incumbent mayor, Shelley Ann Bentley.

This election sees a big change in NiagaraPaul ForsythA collage of election sign clusters along roadways in Niagara Falls. (Paul Forsyth/CBC)I'm Paul Forsyth, a CBC News reporter based in Niagara. I'll be watching what's shaping up to be some interesting election races in this region.One of the biggest changes is there are no choices for regional council for the first time in 56 years, because the Ontario government is eliminating the 19 region-only council positions. That means only the 12 Niagara mayors will sit on regional council, along with a provincially-appointed chair.Thorold, Niagara-on-the-Lake and Lincoln are all guaranteed to get new mayors because their incumbent mayors didn't run for re-election.The same is true in Welland, which has the hottest mayoral race. Eight people are vying to claim the seat left vacant by outgoing Mayor Frank Campion. In smaller Wainfleet, there's even a grudge match: former mayor Kevin Gibson, who was narrowly defeated in 2022 by current Mayor Brian Grant, is the sole challenger to Grant in this election.
